statusDetail: Coverage-complete atomic audit of six representative public paths. Authenticated account management, paid checkout completion and destructive form submission were intentionally not performed; their public entry states and applicable template checks were inspected.

page.notes: Server-rendered Norwegian news publication with an initial cross-origin Sourcepoint/Schibsted consent layer, long feed, article templates, forms, account links, video and ad integrations.

checkOutcomes.method: CDP emulated-media computed-style probe and screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark emulation leaves color-scheme normal and light body colors unchanged.

checkOutcomes.method: getAnimations() comparison under emulated reduced motion
checkOutcomes.evidence: 409 animations remain running under reduce, close to the default 420.
High-contrast screenshot preserves visible text, controls and focus; Lighthouse contrast checks pass.

checkOutcomes.method: Platform/CSS probe and route screenshot comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: No view-transition signal is present across linked MPA templates.
Stylesheet probe found animation-timeline/scroll-timeline use, avoiding a solely scroll-event-driven implementation.
Mobile drawer opens from a labelled button, fits the viewport, and uses native scrolling/expand controls without observed custom pointer friction.

checkOutcomes.method: Long-page visual inspection and CSS probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Long homepage/article surfaces retain static fixed chrome without progress or changed scroll state.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS feature probe plus opened overlay screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Live CSS inspection finds anchor positioning and the inspected mobile menu remains attached and fully visible.
Expanded mobile navigation clearly groups content, shows disclosure state, and keeps the underlying selected content spatially understandable.
Cookie consent obscures nearly all initial desktop and mobile content.
The consent surface is a role=dialog div around a cross-origin iframe rather than native dialog, unlike account dialogs on the page.
After consent, the main viewport is dominated by news cards and headlines; chrome is compact and the mobile menu is only shown on request.
360x800 layout reports scrollWidth 360, horizontal overflow 0 and a viewport meta tag on homepage and article.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS rule probe and paired screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage CSS exposes nine container rules and cards/menu visibly recompose at mobile width.

checkOutcomes.method: Programmatic focus probe, Lighthouse and mobile interaction
checkOutcomes.evidence: Focus probes show a visible browser outline on controls; Lighthouse accessibility is 1.0 and mobile controls are usable in the opened menu.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative first-viewport screenshots and heading probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage, section, article and tips templates expose clear headlines/purpose and labelled next actions.
The public tips journey reaches a labelled POST form with required content and optional contact/file fields without an account wall.
Invalid required content triggers native validation and a real HTTP 404 presents explanation, feedback and homepage recovery links.
Lighthouse mobile LCP is 8.0 s and CLS 0.054; unthrottled trace LCP is 1.89 s, showing slow-condition risk.
Observed CLS is 0 on the homepage consent state and 0.052 on article mobile, both within the good threshold.
Trace reports zero >50 ms long tasks and 0 ms TBT; Lighthouse TBT is 70 ms.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR candidates confirmed against live DOM plus Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: Five confirmed head stylesheets are render-blocking with about 170 ms potential savings.
Lighthouse estimates 464 KiB unused JS, 32 KiB unused CSS, 17 KiB duplicated JS and 40 KiB legacy JS.
Lighthouse accessibility scores 1.0; form fields are labelled or aria-labelled and meaningful article imagery has descriptive alt text.
Lighthouse accessibility and visual checks found no contrast failure, including high-contrast emulation.
Homepage has no h1 and begins with repeated h2 teaser headings, although landmarks and focus outlines exist.
Article body has a comfortable narrow measure and clear typographic hierarchy; mobile headlines reflow without clipping.
Mobile layouts reflow with zero horizontal overflow, scaling is not prevented, Lighthouse accessibility is 1.0, and article audio has a labelled control.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse console audit and HAR hygiene
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse and HAR record repeated 400/403/404 failures plus an Account SDK console.error.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse document checks and image primitives
checkOutcomes.evidence: Doctype/charset pass, but image probes find incomplete dimensions/oversizing and Lighthouse estimates 326 KiB savings.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices audits and initial-load observation
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reports BFCache, deprecations and inspector issues passing; no permission prompt appears on load.
All four templates have descriptive titles and meta descriptions.
Real hrefs, viewport metadata, crawlable robots policy and Lighthouse SEO 1.0 are present.

checkOutcomes.method: Cross-template canonical probe plus robots/sitemap headers
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage, section and article have canonicals and sitemap is 200, but the public tips page has no canonical.

checkOutcomes.method: Metadata probe on representative rich entities
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage/section/article expose JSON-LD and Open Graph; article OG title/image match its visible story.
HTTPS, CSP and HSTS are strong, but __mbl is a 365-day cookie without Secure and _sp_su uses SameSite=None.
82 requests and 2.04 MB transfer are third-party across 26 origins, including a known tracker.
No browser permission prompt fires on load; authentication is delegated to Schibsted and no password/auth data is collected by the audited VG templates.
CSP frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, DENY framing, strict-origin referrer policy and restrictive permissions policy are all present.
Raw HTML retains 96% homepage and 97% article rendered vocabulary; neither page is a JS shell.
Opened mobile menu fits the viewport and remains usable; 404 and template navigation stabilize without blank shells.
A standalone manifest and shortcuts are present but no service-worker registrations exist.
A real 404 status renders an explanatory state with feedback and homepage recovery actions rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM language and responsive visual probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: All templates declare lang=no and preserve natural Norwegian reading order across desktop/mobile; no bidi-sensitive flow is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered content and DOM text inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: News timestamps are rendered in Norwegian relative forms such as “I dag”, “i går”, minutes and hours, consistently across templates.
No user-entered, scheduled, recurring or cross-zone time flow exists in the representative public news, article, tips or offers templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: Covered templates only display publisher-local relative timestamps; there is no cross-zone event-management task to exercise.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Consent UI makes acceptance prominent while personalized-ad rejection is labelled as a paid service and no equal reject-all action appears.
Required tips content uses native post-interaction validity with a specific “Please fill in this field” message; fields are labelled.
Tips contact fields for name, email and telephone have no autocomplete tokens.

checkOutcomes.method: Offer text/link probe and navigation inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: Commercial offers are explicitly labelled ANNONSE and show merchant/discount; account and subscription actions are clearly named and leave VG for their dedicated provider.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse image insight plus image primitives
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 326 KiB image savings and probes identify oversized/missing-dimension assets.
Initial view initiates 152 requests, 94 scripts and 23 fetches, including repeated failed anonymous account calls.
Initial transfer is 2.80 MB, with an 829 KB preview MP4 and 2.04 MB third-party bytes before playback intent.

checkOutcomes.method: Platform probe and declared robots policy
checkOutcomes.evidence: No WebMCP capability is exposed and robots explicitly disallows AI training crawlers while allowing OAI SearchBot.
checkOutcomes.reason: VG expresses a deliberate crawler/licensing policy and no agent-facing transactional capability intent; absence of WebMCP is not penalised.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The covered news, article and tips surfaces do not present a user task that requires site-authored on-device inference.
checkOutcomes.reason: No declared agent/on-device inference intent or applicable user flow was found; browser globals alone do not prove site use.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten bottom-to-top scroll cycles, total self size rose only 6,736 bytes (0.03%) and nodes 0.4%, with no Detached constructor in the top summaries.
Baseline heap is 25.29 MB self size and 398,725 nodes for a very long, media-rich homepage; footprint remained stable after exercise.
Neither heap summary lists Detached constructors among top retained constructors and repeated scroll did not produce material total growth.

principleOutcomes.reason: VG expresses a deliberate crawler/licensing policy and no agent-facing transactional capability intent; absence of WebMCP is not penalised. No declared agent/on-device inference intent or applicable user flow was found; browser globals alone do not prove site use.

paths.description: Homepage/news feed: primary entry template, consent, navigation, preferences, responsive layout, performance and network.
Current news article: representative editorial detail, rich metadata, text, imagery and mobile stability.
Tips submission: primary public form flow, labels, validation and input assistance.
Commercial offers: representative advertising/commercial labelling surface.
Invalid route: HTTP failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: Cookie consent blocks the entire initial experience
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360x800 screenshots show a full-page modal before any interaction; on mobile almost no news content remains visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the least intrusive consent layer permitted, keep core context visible, and provide an immediate, equally legible decline path.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is an ad-hoc iframe dialog rather than a native dialog
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows a div with role=dialog wrapping a cross-origin iframe, while the site uses native dialog elsewhere.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a correctly managed native dialog where integration permits, including focus containment, Escape handling and return focus.

findings.summary: Consent choices are visually asymmetric and decline is framed as paid
findings.evidence: The mobile consent screenshot makes “Godta alle” the prominent first action; “Avvis personlig tilpassede annonser” is marked “Betalt tjeneste”, and there is no equally prominent reject-all option.
findings.suggestedFix: Present accept and reject choices with comparable prominence and explain paid/ad-funded alternatives without steering language.

findings.summary: The site does not honor the system dark-color preference
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, color-scheme remains normal and the body remains rgb(250,246,246) with dark text; the dark screenshot is visually unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface, text, control and media treatments.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference leaves hundreds of animations running
findings.evidence: The probe found 409 running animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, with 200 ms and 1900 ms durations, versus 420 in the default state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use prefers-reduced-motion to remove or substantially reduce non-essential teaser, loading and chrome motion.

findings.summary: Cross-page navigation has no View Transition treatment
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition declaration or API usage across the homepage and article templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for stable shared chrome and directional route changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Sticky site chrome does not communicate scroll state
findings.evidence: Visual inspection and the multi-state probe show a fixed red header but no progress cue, compacted state or other position feedback on long pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll-state treatment or article progress affordance without increasing chrome.

findings.summary: Mobile lab LCP is slow despite a fast unthrottled trace
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.0 s, performance 0.72 and interactive 16.4 s; the unthrottled trace measured LCP 1.89 s, showing a material slow-device/network gap.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical-path work and media, preserve the correctly prioritised LCP image, and validate against mobile throttling and field CWV.

findings.summary: Critical delivery includes avoidable render-blocking CSS
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified five blocking CSS files with about 170 ms potential savings; the DOM confirms they are head stylesheets, while parser-discovered module scripts are correctly deferred by type=module.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline truly critical CSS, consolidate template CSS, and defer non-critical component styles.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial unused and duplicated code
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 464 KiB unused JavaScript, 32 KiB unused CSS, 17 KiB duplicated JavaScript and 40 KiB legacy JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load the video player, ads and CMP branches; deduplicate shared libraries and stop serving legacy transforms to modern clients.

findings.summary: The homepage has no level-one heading
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found zero h1 elements and begins its content outline with many h2 teaser headings; section and article templates do provide h1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one concise, visually appropriate h1 for the homepage content/feed and retain the existing teaser hierarchy beneath it.

findings.summary: Routine account and media checks log browser errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports failed 400/403/404 resources and an Account SDK “HasSession failed” console.error; the HAR independently records the same failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle expected anonymous/geoblocking responses without console errors, and remove or repair the missing bottombar/tracker requests.

findings.summary: Several article and homepage images lack complete intrinsic sizing or are oversized
findings.evidence: The image probes report one homepage image without dimensions, three article images without complete dimensions, and four article assets over 2x display size; Lighthouse estimates 326 KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height for every rendered image and tune sizes/srcset plus compression to actual card and avatar slots.

findings.summary: The public tips page omits a canonical URL
findings.evidence: The tips template has a descriptive title but the probe found no link rel=canonical, unlike the homepage, section and article templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a self-referencing canonical URL to the tips page template.

findings.summary: The initial page has a large third-party and tracking footprint
findings.evidence: The HAR records 82 third-party requests and 2.04 MB third-party transfer across 26 external origins; the tracker probe identifies adnxs and the network includes analytics/ad SDKs.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential third parties until the relevant consent, consolidate measurement, and load video/ad stacks only when their surface is used.

findings.summary: A long-lived first-party cookie is set without Secure
findings.evidence: Cookie inspection found __mbl with a 365-day expiry and Secure=false; _sp_su also uses SameSite=None, although no auth-like cookie lacked HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every cookie delivered by HTTPS and review whether SameSite=None is required for _sp_su.

findings.summary: The app-like manifest is not backed by an offline service worker
findings.evidence: A complete standalone manifest with shortcuts is linked, but the service-worker registration probe returned an empty list.
findings.suggestedFix: If installability is intentional, register a small service worker with a safe offline news shell/fallback; otherwise avoid implying full PWA capability.

findings.summary: The tips form omits autocomplete assistance for contact fields
findings.evidence: The publicly accessible form labels its name, email and telephone inputs correctly but all three have empty autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Add name, email and tel autocomplete tokens so browsers and assistive input tools can help users submit tips.

findings.summary: Responsive image delivery leaves avoidable bytes on the table
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 326 KiB image savings, including 1080 px assets displayed around 665 px and a 552 px PNG displayed around 74 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct sizes/srcset candidates, use AVIF/WebP where the image service permits, and compress campaign graphics for their rendered slot.

findings.summary: Initial background work is disproportionate to the news view
findings.evidence: The homepage initiates 152 requests, including 94 scripts and 23 fetch/XHR requests; several anonymous account checks fail repeatedly.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay account, ad, analytics and player work until needed, batch telemetry, and remove repeated failed fetches.

findings.summary: Autoloaded media and third-party code dominate the initial budget
findings.evidence: The HAR transfers 2.80 MB total, including an 829 KB preview MP4 and 2.04 MB from third parties before the user requests playback.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace autoplay preview transfer with a poster, fetch media on intent, and set explicit third-party/media budgets.

taskList.title: Replace the blocking, asymmetric consent experience with balanced choices
Cut initial third-party, video and unused-code work
Meet mobile LCP and critical-delivery budgets
Add preference-driven dark and reduced-motion modes
Repair semantic structure, autocomplete and canonical details
Eliminate routine console/network errors and harden cookies
Complete image sizing and responsive delivery
Add progressive route transitions and scroll-state guidance
Back the app manifest with a safe offline fallback
